import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_4/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_4/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_4/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_4/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Merge source0 and source1 on 'Artist' (JOIN operation)
df_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='Artist', how='left')

# Step 2: Merge the result with source3 on 'Artist' (JOIN operation)
df_013 = pd.merge(df_01, source3, on='Artist', how='left')

# Step 3: Merge the above result with source2 on 'Artist' (JOIN operation)
# source2 has overlapping columns: 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated'
# We want to fill missing values in df_013 from source2 where possible
df_final = pd.merge(df_013, source2, on='Artist', how='left', suffixes=('', '_src2'))

# For columns that exist in both df_013 and source2, fill missing values in df_final from source2 columns
for col in ['Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']:
    col_src2 = col + '_src2'
    # Convert to numeric to handle possible NaNs and type consistency
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce')
    df_final[col_src2] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col_src2], errors='coerce')
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].combine_first(df_final[col_src2])
    df_final.drop(columns=[col_src2], inplace=True)

# The column 'Certified Units (Millions)' appears twice after merging source3:
# In df_013, it is named 'Certified Units (Millions)' from source3
# In df_01, it was missing, so no suffix needed.
# After merging with source2, no new 'Certified Units (Millions)' columns added.
# So keep 'Certified Units (Millions)' as is.

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types:
# Target Schema: ['Artist': string, 'Year Inducted': float, 'Years Waited': int,
# '# of Years Nominated': int, 'Inducted By': string, 'Influenced': int,
# 'Certified Units (Millions)': float]

# Cast columns to correct types
df_final['Artist'] = df_final['Artist'].astype(str)

# 'Year Inducted' float (NaNs allowed)
df_final['Year Inducted'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['Year Inducted'], errors='coerce')

# 'Years Waited' integer (NaNs to be kept as NaN, but pandas int dtype with NaNs requires Int64)
df_final['Years Waited'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['Years Waited'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# '# of Years Nominated' integer
df_final['# of Years Nominated'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['# of Years Nominated'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Inducted By' string, keep NaNs as is
df_final['Inducted By'] = df_final['Inducted By'].replace({np.nan: None})
df_final['Inducted By'] = df_final['Inducted By'].astype('string')

# 'Influenced' integer
df_final['Influenced'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['Influenced'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Certified Units (Millions)' float
df_final['Certified Units (Millions)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['Certified Units (Millions)'], errors='coerce')

# Select only the target columns in order
target_columns = ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated',
                  'Inducted By', 'Influenced', 'Certified Units (Millions)']

Target5_4 = df_final[target_columns]

# Write the final dataframe to the specified path without the index
Target5_4.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on Artist (left join to keep all artists from Source0)
df = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Artist", how="left")

# Join the result with Source2 on Artist (left join to keep all artists from Source0)
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="Artist", how="left", suffixes=('', '_src2'))

# The columns Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated appear in both source0 and source2.
# We want to keep the values from source0 primarily, but fill missing values from source2.
for col in ["Year Inducted", "Years Waited", "# of Years Nominated"]:
    df[col] = df[col].combine_first(df[f"{col}_src2"])
    df.drop(columns=[f"{col}_src2"], inplace=True)

# Join the result with Source3 on Artist (left join)
df = pd.merge(df, source3, on="Artist", how="left")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns that are unique identifiers in target:
# According to target schema and hints, group by:
# Artist (string), Year Inducted (float, exclude from group by), Years Waited (int), # of Years Nominated (int), Inducted By (string)
# Year Inducted is float, so exclude from group by.
# So group by: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By
# But target examples show Year Inducted is float and present, so we keep it as group by attribute only if it is not float.
# Hint 6 says do not group by float columns.
# So group by: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By
# But target examples show Year Inducted is float and present, so we keep it as group by attribute only if it is not float.
# So group by: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By
# But the target schema leftmost columns are: Artist (string), Year Inducted (float), Years Waited (int), # of Years Nominated (int), Inducted By (string)
# Year Inducted is float, exclude from group by.
# So group by: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By

# However, the target examples show Year Inducted is sometimes NaN, so grouping by it is not good.
# So group by: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By

# But Inducted By is string, and likely unique per artist, so include it.

# To be safe, also include Year Inducted in group by because it is part of the key in target examples (some artists have same name but different year? Unlikely)
# But since it is float, exclude it.

# So final group by columns: Artist, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By

# Aggregations: sum Influenced, sum Certified Units (Millions)
# Fill NaNs in aggregation columns with 0 before sum

df["Influenced"] = df["Influenced"].fillna(0)
df["Certified Units (Millions)"] = df["Certified Units (Millions)"].fillna(0)

grouped = df.groupby(["Artist", "Years Waited", "# of Years Nominated", "Inducted By"], dropna=False).agg({
    "Year Inducted": "first",  # Year Inducted is float, take first non-null value
    "Influenced": "sum",
    "Certified Units (Millions)": "sum"
}).reset_index()

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[[
    "Artist",
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Inducted By",
    "Influenced",
    "Certified Units (Millions)"
]]

# Write to output CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
